analysis.overall: You spent 90% of your day in range with a flat overnight trend, though stacked correction doses in the early afternoon led to a low and a temporary rebound high.

events.title: Afternoon correction stack
events.description: Taking several small correction doses in quick succession caused glucose to fall continuously over two hours, hitting a low of 56 mg/dL.

events.title: Rebound peak after treatment
events.description: Treating the low with carbs alongside additional insulin doses triggered a sharp spike up to 213 mg/dL before settling back down.

events.title: Dinner rise and return
events.description: A 30g carb meal pushed numbers up to 195 mg/dL, but a series of small corrections helped bring you safely back into target before bed.

events.title: Steady overnight baseline
events.description: Your levels remained remarkably stable in the 70–100 mg/dL range through the entire night.

events.title: Breakfast bump
events.description: A 40g carb breakfast caused a brief rise to 182 mg/dL, which resolved smoothly back down to ~120 mg/dL within 90 minutes.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Giving correction boluses more time to work before giving follow-up doses can help avoid late-afternoon lows and sudden rebound spikes.
